གང་ཞེ་ན། ཆོས་འདི་བཤད་པ་དང་། མཉན་པར་དཀའ་བའོ། །དེ་ལ་བཤད་པར་དཀའ་བ་#ཉིད་ཅེས་བསྟན་པའི་ཕྱིར། འདི་ནི་དཀའ་བ་དམ་པ་རྨད་བྱུང་བ། །བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་རབ་བསྟན་པ། །ས་རྒྱུ་རྣམ་པར་དབྱེ་བ་མཆོག་ཡིན་ཏེ། །དེ་ལས་སངས་རྒྱས་དངོས་པོ་ཡང་དག་འཐོབ། །
ཅེས་བྱ་བ་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་ལ་དཀའ་བ་ནི་བསྒྲུབ་#དཀའ་བའོ། །དཀའ་བ་ཉིད་རྣམ་པ་གཉིས་ཏེ། ཤིན་ཏུ་དཀའ་བ་ཉིད་དང་། མ་འདྲིས་པས་དཀའ་བ་ཉིད་དོ། །དེ་ནི་དམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། རྨད་དུ་བྱུང་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བསྟན་ཏོ། །ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་#དེ་ལྟར་དཀའ་ཞེ་ན། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་སྤྱོད་པ་རབ་བསྟན་

span: It is the fact that this Dharma is difficult to explain and difficult to hear. To show that it is difficult to explain, he said: "This is the supreme and marvelous difficulty, the fully revealed conduct of the Bodhisattvas, the supreme classification of the grounds and causes, from which the state of a Buddha is truly obtained." In that regard, "difficulty" means difficult to accomplish. There are two types of difficulty: the difficulty of extreme hardship and the difficulty of unfamiliarity. These are shown by "supreme" and "marvelous." If one asks why it is so difficult: "The fully revealed conduct of the Bodhisattvas, the supreme classification of the grounds and causes." In that regard, the "conduct of the Bodhisattvas" is the primordial wisdom of realization. Because it fully shows that, it is "fully revealed." "The supreme classification of the grounds and causes" means that the teaching of the levels, which are the causes of the Bodhisattva's conduct, is the ultimate perfection. What is the conduct of the Bodhisattvas like? He said: "From which the state of a Buddha is truly obtained." The "state of a Buddha" is Buddhahood itself, the primordial wisdom of a Buddha. Having shown the difficulty of explaining, he shows the cause of why it is difficult. What is its cause? It is that the meaning of the Bodhisattva's conduct cannot be explained exactly as it exists. If one asks how that meaning exists: "Fine in parts, difficult to see, abandoning conceptualization; because it is free from the ground of the mind, it is difficult to accomplish. It is the untainted sphere of the wise; if the world hears it, they will be deluded by it." In that regard, "difficulty of accomplishment" is the limb. The rest are secondary limbs. Regarding that, "difficult to accomplish" means difficult to obtain, which means difficult to realize. That difficulty of accomplishment is of four types, from "difficult to accomplish because it is fine in parts" up to "difficult to accomplish because it is free from the ground of the mind." In that regard, "fine in parts" means it is not something to be known by wisdom arising from hearing, for the coarse is not something to be known without needing contemplation. "Difficult to see"
tail: means it is not something to be known even by what arises from contemplation.
old_translation:
What is that which is to be understood? It is this Dharma which is difficult to explain and difficult to hear. To show that it is "difficult to explain," it is said:

This is the supreme and marvelous difficulty,
The perfectly shown conduct of the Bodhisattva,
The supreme division of the cause which is the stages,
From which the state of a Buddha is truly obtained.

Regarding this, "difficulty" means difficulty in accomplishment. Difficulty itself is of two kinds: extreme difficulty and difficulty due to lack of familiarity. These are shown by "supreme" and "marvelous." 

If one asks: why is it so difficult? It is as said: "The perfectly shown conduct of the Bodhisattva, the supreme division of the cause which is the stages." Here, the "conduct of the Bodhisattvas" is the wisdom of realization. Because it demonstrates that, it is "perfectly shown." "The supreme division of the cause which is the stages" means the explanation of the stages, which are the cause of the Bodhisattva's conduct, is the true culmination. 

If one asks: what is the conduct of the Bodhisattva like? It says: "From which the state of a Buddha is truly obtained." The "state of a Buddha" is Buddhahood itself, the wisdom of a Buddha. Having shown the difficulty of explanation, he shows the cause of that difficulty. What is that cause? It is the inability to explain the meaning of the Bodhisattva's conduct exactly as it stays.

If one asks: how does that meaning stay? It is as said:
Subtle, hard to see, abandoning conceptions,
Difficult to accomplish because it is free from the ground of mind;
The stainless sphere of the wise,
The world, having heard it, becomes deluded.

Here, "difficulty in accomplishment" is the primary limb. The rest are secondary limbs. Difficulty in accomplishment means difficulty in attainment or difficulty in realization. This difficulty is of four types, from "difficulty due to subtlety" to "difficulty because it is free from the ground of mind." Regarding "subtle," it is not something to be known by wisdom arising from hearing. "Hard to see" means it is not to be known by wisdom arising from reflection. "Abandoning conceptions" means it is not to be known by wisdom arising from mundane meditation, for "conceptions" are the minds and mental factors of the three realms. This shows it is not the sphere of knowledge arising from mundane application. "Free from the ground of mind" shows it is not even the sphere of the specific mind arising from the maturation of what is obtained at birth. Here, "ground of mind" should be understood as the sphere of the mind.

If one asks: whose sphere is it then? It says: "The stainless sphere of the wise." This means those who have seen the truth. Why not others? Because it is "stainless," meaning it is supramundane. Therefore, it is not to be known by mundane knowledge. Thus, even if one explains that profound meaning as best as one can, it remains difficult: "The world, having heard it, becomes deluded." 
How are they deluded? By grasping at the meaning exactly according to the literal sound. "Having heard it" refers to the difficulty of explaining it after it has been heard.
